findings.title: Modelling note: DBMF's T-bill part is taxed as a deferred gain, the TBILL asset as yearly income
findings.evidence: df7.py:80 sets DBMF to (rf + TR - fee, INC=0, HV=1), so its T-bill yield is taxed only when gains are realised. TBILL has HV=2, so its whole return is taxed each year at 15.4%. The spec does not cover this. The treatment matches DF5's zero-excess assets (for example GOLD). Not quantified. It slightly favours DBMF-heavy rules and the M100/MGT off-states over the BILL off-state. It is very unlikely to turn any rule into a G1-G5 passer: the nearest misses fail on p10 or drawdown gates.

findings.title: job7 and dfk timing: signal at close t, trade 2 days later, rebalance every 252 days; no look-ahead found
findings.evidence: T200 and M252 recomputed from path data up to close t: 0 mismatches. Synthetic dfk test: when the target changes at close d, the new holdings first earn day d+3's return, so the trade happens at close d+2. A forced rebalance (k%252==0) re-applies the most recent decided weights from no later than t-2 (dfk.py:47-54). REAL trade counts match the expected union of first trade, signal flips and forced dates exactly: F3 T200 250 trades (222 flips), F3|M252|Q50M50|BILL 201, static P2 30 (1 + 29 annual). The trend proxy's weights use data up to t-1 and are applied to day t, rebalanced weekly (df7.py:40-42). Only the very first allocation has a 1-day lag (W[WARM-1] traded at close WARM). This is the DF5 engine convention and applies to QQQ too.

findings.title: final(): H1/H3/H4/H5, tiers, neighbours, selection, tie rule, f* and report sets match the spec
findings.evidence: H1: cost 0.006 for both the rule and QQQ, on REAL (single path), P30 and X30. H3: P125 over 30 years with the G2 conditions. H4: F1/F2 neighbours are same-family points within 0.1 on every weight including DBMF (Chebyshev distance), needing at least 4 neighbours with at least 75% passing; F3 needs its twin with the other signal to pass G1-G5. H5: G1-G5 under Q. Tier 1 needs everything; tier 2 fails only H5. The neighbour score is the minimum over the rule and all its neighbours, passing or not; the answer is the highest; ties within 0.0005 go to the largest minimum drawdown margin. f* is the smallest trend fraction (0 to 1.0 in 0.05 steps, neutral panel) at which G1-G5 pass. Reports cover the answer or the family bests, plus P2 and P3, under PRIM/RAW/ZERO for REAL, P/X 5/10/20/30 and P125. Notes that change nothing: tier 1 is tried before tier 2 (implied, not written, in the spec). 'Family best' is chosen by (gate count, score), the DF5 convention, which the spec does not define. f* is computed for the family bests and P2, more than the spec requires, and not for P3. The v1/v2 rows the spec wants in the user table are not produced by df7.py and must come from the DF5/DF6 results.

findings.title: No look-ahead in trend_by_date; source end dates and pre-start NaNs handled correctly
findings.evidence: df7.py:33-43. I re-implemented the proxy separately and it matches exactly (max |diff| of tr and w = 0). Perturbation test: I changed all excess returns from t0 on, for 12 random t0; positions up to and including t0 did not change (max diff 0) and positions after t0 did. Order of steps: the signal (63/126/252-day sign), the 60-day vol and N use data through t; shift(1) moves them to t+1; the weekly keep/ffill comes after the shift. The 3x cap never binds. Every source ends on 2014-12-31 (L._src assert; DD._csv cut at END). On the REAL and P/X calendars, tr has 0 NaN. Before a series starts it stays NaN, so ok=False and w=0. GOLD enters 1986-01-09 and DEVX 1991-07-02 (1990-07-02 + 252 days). N goes from 4 to 5 and the 1/sqrt(N) rule rescales the others. USD has 7 in-range NaNs, all in 1984-85, set to 0 before scoring.

findings.title: Excess returns over the T-bill are built correctly; rf is not double-counted
findings.evidence: Series definitions (df5 MANIFEST), all USD daily simple total returns. LTT: synthetic 25y par bond TR from ^TYX until 2002-07, then TLT TR; no roll-down, no fee. GOLD: spot XAU (price = TR) until 2004-11, then GLD TR. USD: synthetic fully collateralized USDX future (DXY spot change + KF RF + DXY-weighted 3m rate differential) until 2007-03, then UUP TR, net of a 0.75% fee. DEVX: KF Developed ex US market (Mkt-RF+RF, USD, unhedged) from 1990-07 until 2001-08, then EFA TR. Each market enters as ex = TR - rf, so USD-rf = spot change plus carry, which a futures trend fund could earn. The products count rf once: TREND/DBMF = rf + Σw·ex and RSST = SPX TR + Σw·ex (df7.py:79-81). Minor mismatches: (1) DEVX is unhedged, so it carries a long-foreign-currency position; corr(DEVX ex, USD ex) = -0.38, i.e. FX exposure overlaps with the USD market. (2) GOLD spot - rf ignores the lease rate. Both are small.

findings.title: results/df7_trend_stats.json reproduced exactly
findings.evidence: Max diff vs the JSON = 0.0; annual returns match to 4 dp. 1986-2014: mean 10.11%, vol 12.99%, Sharpe 0.778, CAGR 9.70%. 1986-1999: 11.90%, 11.93%, Sharpe 0.997. 2000-2014: 8.43%, 13.90%, Sharpe 0.606. Correlation with NDX: -0.032 daily, +0.055 monthly. Correlation with SPX: -0.040 daily, +0.144 monthly. Mean gross leverage 1.84. In the worst 10% of NDX months (NDX mean -12.6%/month) the proxy averaged +1.77%/month, vs +0.74% in other months.

findings.title: Proxy mean sits at the top of its own implementation band: same-close fill, luckiest weekly phase, no trading costs
findings.evidence: Positions are formed at the same close that the signal reads. One extra day of lag cuts the 1986-2014 mean from 10.11% to 9.01% (Sharpe 0.78 to 0.69); most of the loss is in 1986-1992, spread over SPX, USD and GOLD. With daily rebalancing the extra lag costs 0.8%/yr. The weekly offset used (0) is the best of 5 offsets, which give 8.99-10.11% (average 9.56%). Turnover is 21.6x notional per year, so trading costs of 2/5/10 bp per unit traded would be 0.43/1.08/2.16%/yr; the proxy has none. A realistic implementable gross is about 8.0-9.2%/yr. Under PRIM the shift is proportional to the proxy mean, so the absolute PRIM premium would fall about 10% (5.05% to about 4.5%). That changes nothing, because PRIM already has 0 passes. RAW (100%) rows (step A, report) are an upper bound.

findings.title: USD source days on NYSE holidays are dropped instead of compounded
findings.evidence: 143 USD source days fall off the NYSE calendar (1985-2007, about 8 per year, mostly Mondays). trend_by_date reindexes, so these days are dropped; the same happens in DD._on_cal. Their simple returns sum to +5.3%. Compounding them into the next NYSE day changes the 1986-2014 proxy mean from 10.11% to 10.18% (Sharpe 0.778 to 0.784). Negligible.

findings.title: P&L decomposition: the bond bull is a minor source; most of the return is timing, plus equity drift
findings.evidence: Annualized contributions, 1986-2014 (total 10.11%): SPX 1.96, LTT 1.67, GOLD 2.47, USD 2.33, DEVX 1.67. 1986-1999 (total 11.90%): SPX 2.08, LTT 3.45, GOLD 3.09, USD 2.74, DEVX 0.54. 2000-2014 (total 8.43%): SPX 1.85, LTT 0.00, GOLD 1.89, USD 1.95, DEVX 2.73. 2009-2014 (total 7.73%): SPX 2.96, LTT 1.04, GOLD 3.25, USD 0.86, DEVX -0.39. Bond bull: the 30y yield went 9.27% (1985), 6.48% (1999), 2.75% (2014). Long LTT positions earned +2.18%/yr and shorts -0.51%/yr; LTT net was 16.5% of the proxy mean (29% in 1986-1999, 0% in 2000-2014). The pure LTT drift part is 0.84%/yr. Zeroing LTT drift and recomputing signals cuts the mean only from 10.1% to 9.31%. Drift vs timing, 1986-2014: drift 3.0%/yr (SPX 2.0%; long SPX 73% of days), timing 7.1%/yr. Zero-drift counterfactuals (demeaned excess, signals recomputed): LTT and GOLD 9.36%; LTT, GOLD and USD 8.79%; all five markets 6.05% (Sharpe 0.47) for 1986-2014, 3.99% for 2000-2014 and 2.22% for 2009-2014. In 2009-2014 timing was -0.2%/yr; that period's 7.7% came from long-equity and long-gold drift.

findings.title: AQR TSMOM comparison and fee estimate: a fee-paying fund keeps about 50-65% of the proxy premium (estimate)
findings.evidence: Monthly, 1986-2014: AQR mean 15.3%, vol 11.9%, Sharpe 1.28 vs proxy 10.1%, 12.7%, 0.80; corr 0.573. 1986-1999: AQR Sharpe 1.58 vs proxy 0.94, corr 0.50. 2000-2014: 1.04 vs 0.66, corr 0.64. 2009-2014: 0.55 vs 0.61, corr 0.61. The AQR Sharpe decays steadily. AQR sector Sharpes 2009-2014: FI 0.74, CM/EQ/FX 0.17-0.19. Fee estimate (not a fund record): both series scaled to 13% vol, then 2% management + 20% performance with a monthly high-water mark. Proxy, 1986-2014: gross 10.3%; net 6.8% with the performance fee over a T-bill hurdle and no cost (66% kept); net 5.3% with no hurdle and 1%/yr trading cost (51% kept). AQR: gross 16.7%; net 11.8% (71% kept) and 10.3% (62% kept). In 2000-2014 the proxy nets 4.1-5.3% and AQR 8.7-9.8%; in 2009-2014 the proxy nets 4.0-5.0% and AQR 3.5-4.3%. The AQR gross Sharpe of 1.28 is likely well above what real fee-paying CTAs delivered. Real CTA index data was not obtainable (MANIFEST), so that is unverified.

findings.title: PRIM (50% of proxy mean = 5.05%/yr before the 0.85% fee; 4.2% net; Sharpe after fee 0.32) is fair to mildly optimistic, not pessimistic; f* of 0.70-0.80 needs an optimistic premium
findings.evidence: 5.05% is about the in-sample result of running the proxy as a 2/20 fund with 1% costs (5.3%). It is 55-63% of the implementable gross (8.0-9.2%). Factors pointing down: AQR Sharpe decay (1.58, 1.04, 0.55); timing of about zero in 2009-2014; the zero-drift proxy earns only 4.0% gross in 2000-2014, before costs; bond-bull drift cannot repeat from a 2.75% yield (only about 0.8-1.7%/yr of the proxy); and post-publication decay of trend premia (magnitude unverified). Factors pointing up: the proxy has only 5 markets while AQR's 58-market version has a much higher gross Sharpe; and DBMF's fee is 0.85%, not 2/20. The manager's claim that replication recovers pre-fee returns is unverified. Q (25%, 1.7% net) is a reasonable pessimistic case. df7_final.json: PRIM G1-G5 passes = 0, tier 1 = 0, tier 2 = 0, no selection. f* = 0.70 for the best F2 (F2|q0.2|r0.7|g0.1|m0.0) and 0.80 for user P2. These need 7.1-8.1% pre-fee excess at 13% vol, i.e. the 2000-2014 gross proxy repeating with essentially no haircut. The calibration therefore supports the 0-pass headline. No pass count, tier, selection, f* or headline changes.
